preconditioning.notes: Estimated: BMW iX release says "anticipatory thermal management enables the high-voltage battery's operating temperature to be optimised" (same wording as the i4, whose US page spells out the navigation trigger; manual control not addressed).

chemistry.notes: Estimated: BMW US page for this pack says the cathode cobalt share was cut to below ten percent (a cobalt-bearing nickel-manganese-cobalt type cathode; the page does not name NMC).

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: same hardware as MY2022 (the page read); model years compared 2022 to 2025, nothing shows a change. ArenaEV iX xDrive50 page: "400V" (BMW iX pages do not state voltage).

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: same hardware as MY2022 (the page read); model years compared 2022 to 2025, nothing shows a change. BMW global: xDrive50 net 105.2 kWh. M60 shares the pack (model notes). 2022-2025 compared: no change named.

capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Estimated: same hardware as MY2022 (the page read); model years compared 2022 to 2025, nothing shows a change. BMW global: gross 111.5 kWh.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: same hardware as MY2022 (the page read); model years compared 2022 to 2025, nothing shows a change. BMW global release: up to 200 kW (xDrive50). Other listings state 195 kW for US cars.

Estimated: same hardware as MY2022 (the page read); model years compared 2022 to 2025, nothing shows a change. BMW Ireland table lists 195 kW for the xDrive50 (provisional); InsideEVs also says BMW rates the xDrive50 at 195 kW.

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: same hardware as MY2022 (the page read); model years compared 2022 to 2025, nothing shows a change. BMW global: Flexible Fast Charger up to 11 kW.

published_10_80_min.notes: Estimated: same hardware as MY2022 (the page read); model years compared 2022 to 2025, nothing shows a change. BMW global: 10-80 % around 35 min (xDrive50).
